improvementsForChallenger: Replace the abstract dark-teal polygon clumps at the field edges with resolved environment props (shaded trees, rocks, flower clusters); in every corner crop they currently read as unfinished masking shapes, not a meadow.
Remove or drastically soften the heavy dark corner vignette; it muddies the olive ground into dirty gradients and fights the 'sunlit meadow' brief instead of framing it.
Give cards physical presence: add edge thickness, a visible stacked pile for deck/grave zones, and warmer, tighter contact shadows so cards stop floating on a flat color field.
Add ground micro-detail to the play surface (grass texture, scattered petals, mow-band variation, subtle noise); the flat mustard fill between cards reads as a UI background, not terrain.
Integrate the divider into the world: let its light spill onto the ground and introduce slight organic irregularity; the current perfectly straight beam reads as a plastic strip laid over the scene.
Ground the cards: add soft contact shadows and slight stack thickness under decks and creatures so they stop floating on flat color and appear to rest on the field
Replace the abstract corner polygon blobs with readable environment props; the bottom-left and bottom-right corner crops are currently illegible overlapping flat shapes with no silhouette logic
Break up the flat olive ground with texture and life: subtle grass mottling, flower clusters, or tonal variation so the play surface reads as meadow rather than a solid fill
Establish a light direction: the dark vignette currently reads as smudge; convert it into believable foliage shade with a warm sun-side gradient and consistent shadowing on props
Give the divider material presence: the bare thin line with a diamond reads as UI, not battlefield; add a soft glow, ground interaction, or embossed treatment so it belongs to the world
